subject: Archaeology
title: ROVs and AUVs: Robots in the Deep
description: A quick, practical guide to ROVs and AUVs: Robots in the Deep.

hook.text: Robots now explore shipwrecks at depths where humans cannot survive — mapping sites no diver will ever reach.

buildup.text: ROVs (Remotely Operated Vehicles) are tethered robots with cameras and manipulator arms controlled from the surface.

discovery.text: AUVs (Autonomous Underwater Vehicles) swim independently, scanning vast areas of seabed with sonar and cameras.

twist.text: An AUV found the Endurance at 10,000 feet. It operated under Antarctic ice where no human could have searched.

climax.text: Deep-sea robots are discovering wrecks faster than archaeologists can study them. The technology outpaces the workforce.

punchline.text: Robots can now find wrecks anywhere. The hard part is having enough humans to study them.

quiz.question: What is the difference between ROVs and AUVs?
options: ROVs work only in freshwater while AUVs work in saltwater
ROVs are tethered and controlled from the surface; AUVs swim independently
ROVs are used for photography while AUVs are used for excavation
